questions.question: In this paper what compound does the abbreviation 'NBP' refer to?
What is the structure/product identity of compound 2a formed from 1a under the reported conditions?
questions.ground_truth_answer: Compound 2a is γ-butyrolactone (the 5-membered lactone derived from 1,4-butanediol).

questions.question: What solvent, catalyst(s) and temperature were used in the optimized reaction conditions to convert 1a to 2a (the conditions giving the highest yield)?
questions.ground_truth_answer: Optimized conditions: solvent = toluene; catalysts/additives = Fe(NO3)3·9H2O (10 mol%), TEMPO (10 mol%), KCl (10 mol%); temperature = rt (25 °C) under O2.

questions.question: Which gave the higher NMR yield for formation of 2a: entry 1 (using DCE as solvent) or entry 7 (using toluene) in Table 1?
questions.ground_truth_answer: Entry 7 (toluene) gave the higher yield: 87% NMR yield (81% isolated) vs entry 1 (DCE) 59% NMR yield.

questions.question: What isolated yield is reported for the synthesis of NBP (compound 2q) in Scheme 3?
questions.ground_truth_answer: NBP (2q) was delivered in 70% isolated yield.
